patches.name: JavaScript
patches.summary: Runs a JavaScript file whose code declares its own inputs and outputs, for logic other patches can't express.
patches.behavior:
**Script file.** Setting `script` names a key of `doc.scripts`, such as `"email_check.js"` (stored at `scripts/email_check.js`). Empty means no script: no ports, nothing runs, and the inspector offers "Create script". Tools add `.js` to a name without an extension, and the name must pass core's `isValidScriptFile`. When the editor or MCP inserts a JavaScript patch without a script, it first writes a starter file `<patchId>.js` (or `<patchId>_2.js`, and so on, when taken) with `setScript`, then sets `script`. Duplicating a patch copies its file under a new name. Two patches may point at one file on purpose; editing it changes both.

**Script contract.** The file is one ES module in strict mode:
```js
export const inputs = [{ key: "count", name: "Count", type: "number", default: 0 }];
export const outputs = [{ key: "label", type: "text" }];
export const variants = ["number", "point"];   // optional
export const alwaysEvaluate = false;           // optional
export function evaluate(patch) { patch.output("label", String(patch.input("count"))); }
```
- The four declarations are the header. They must precede every other statement and hold literal values (`dynamicPortsRule`). Each is optional.
- `evaluate` is any export with that name holding a function: a declaration, an arrow, or an `async` function. Without it, only top-level code, timers, and promise callbacks run.
- `import`, `export ... from`, and dynamic `import()` throw "Scripts are one file. Paste the code you need into this file." Top-level `await` throws "Use await inside evaluate or a callback."

**Isolation.**
- Each instance runs in its own context of an isolated JavaScript engine compiled to WebAssembly (reference: QuickJS through `quickjs-emscripten`), with one engine runtime per patch node shared by its instances. Never run script code in the host realm (`eval`, `new Function`, a `<script>` tag, Node `vm`): none of them keep host objects out of reach.
- Globals: the standard ECMAScript built-ins plus `patch`, `console`, `setTimeout`, `clearTimeout`, `setInterval`, `clearInterval`, `queueMicrotask`, `fetch`, `AbortController`, `btoa`, `atob`, `TextEncoder` and `TextDecoder` (UTF-8 only), and `performance.now()`. There is no `window`, `document`, storage, worker, `process`, `require`, or file system, and no access to the document, layers, or other patches.
- Determinism: `Math.random()` calls `ctx.services.random()`. `Date.now()` and `new Date()` with no arguments use `ctx.services.now()`, and `performance.now()` returns `ctx.time * 1000`.
- Values cross the boundary as copies of plain data, so a script can never mutate engine values.
- Budgets: one invocation is running the module top level, one timer callback, one delivery-and-microtask drain, or `evaluate` plus its drain. In the live viewer an invocation may use 50 ms of wall-clock time. Deterministic runtimes count the engine's interrupt checks against a fixed limit instead, so a runaway script stops at the same place every run (a 1 s wall-clock backstop catches unusually slow native work). The budget reaches inside built-ins too: regular expressions run on a budgeted matcher rather than V8's uninterruptible backtracking, so `/^(a+)+$/` on a long near-match stops like a runaway loop, and bulk built-ins (Array, typed array and ArrayBuffer constructors, `fill`, `concat`, `flat`, `sort`, `split`, `JSON.parse`, key enumeration, spread) charge what they would allocate and how many elements they would visit before they run. One invocation may project 64 MB of such allocations, and one native call may visit 64 million elements. Going over aborts the invocation with "The script took too long. Check for a loop that never ends." or "The script used too much memory." It also marks the instance stalled, and a stalled instance doesn't run again until the source changes or the prototype restarts.
- Known gaps: scripts run in Sonobe's in-process interpreter, not the reference QuickJS isolate, so budgets are cooperative. Memory is projected per invocation from what built-ins would allocate, not measured, so memory a script keeps across invocations isn't capped, and a projection is an upper bound (filling one huge array several times in one invocation can stop early).

**State per instance** (one per loop index in per-item mode, or one per patch in whole-loop mode; see Loops):
```
{ source, typeParam, vm, firstRun: true, stalled: false, compileError: null,
  outputs: Map<key, Value>,    // last committed value per declared output
  pulses: Set<key>,            // pulse outputs fired this frame
  previous: Map<key, Value>,   // last frame's converted inputs
  timers: [],                  // { id, seq, due, interval | null, callback, args, notBeforeFrame }
  requests: [],                // { id, seq, settledBeforeFrame | null, result, aborted }
  wantsNextFrame: false, logged: Set<string>, warned: Set<string> }
```

Each frame, per instance:
```
const file = ctx.node.settings?.script ?? "";
const source = file ? ctx.services.readScript(file) : undefined;
if (source === undefined) return;                             // no ports, nothing to output
if (state.source !== source || state.typeParam !== ctx.typeParam) rebuild(state, source);
                                                              // dispose, new context, run top level, firstRun = true
if (ctx.node.muted) { bypass(); return; }                     // see Muted
const inputs = convertDeclaredInputs(ctx);                    // Conversions
const triggered = state.firstRun || header.alwaysEvaluate || state.wantsNextFrame
  || declaredInputs.some((p) => p.type === "pulse" ? ctx.pulsed(p.key) : !deepEqual(inputs.get(p.key), state.previous.get(p.key)));
state.wantsNextFrame = false;
if (!state.stalled && !state.compileError) {
  runDueTimers();              // due <= ctx.time and notBeforeFrame <= ctx.frame, ordered by (due, seq)
  deliverSettledRequests();    // settled before this frame began, ordered by seq
  drainMicrotasks();
  if (triggered && evaluateExport) { callEvaluate(patch); drainMicrotasks(); }
}
for (const p of declaredOutputs) {
  if (p.type === "pulse") { if (state.pulses.has(p.key)) ctx.pulse(p.key); }
  else ctx.output(p.key, state.outputs.has(p.key) ? state.outputs.get(p.key) : defaultOrZero(p));
}
state.pulses.clear(); state.previous = inputs; state.firstRun = false;
if (state.timers.length || state.requests.length || state.wantsNextFrame) ctx.requestNextFrame();
```

**The `patch` object.** It's a global, and the same object is passed to `evaluate`.
- `patch.input(key)`: this frame's value of a declared input (Conversions). In whole-loop mode it returns the first item, or the zero value for an empty loop.
- `patch.inputItems(key)`: every item as an array. In per-item mode, a one-item array.
- `patch.pulsed(key)`: `ctx.pulsed(key)`, true on an upstream pulse or a false-to-true edge of a connected boolean, so a held `true` counts once. Pulses on consecutive frames each count.
- `patch.changed(key)`: true when the value differs from last frame's value for this instance; false on the instance's first frame.
- `patch.isConnected(key)`: `ctx.isConnected(key)`.
- `patch.output(key, value)`: stages a value for a declared output. On a pulse output, a truthy value fires the pulse. Staged writes commit when the invocation returns (Errors).
- `patch.pulse(key)`: fires a declared pulse output this frame. Several calls in one frame make one pulse.
- `patch.requestNextFrame()`: runs `evaluate` next frame even when nothing changed.
- Read-only: `patch.id` (`ctx.id`), `patch.time` and `patch.dt` in seconds, `patch.frame`, `patch.loopIndex`, `patch.loopCount`, and `patch.typeParam` (the active variant, or `null`).
- An undeclared key throws an Error with a did-you-mean and the declared keys, for example: `"lable" isn't an output of this script. Did you mean "label"? Outputs: label, count.` Calling `patch.pulse` on a non-pulse output throws.

**Conversions, engine to script.**
- number and index: a number. boolean: a boolean. pulse: a boolean, the same as `patch.pulsed`. text: a string. enum: the option key.
- json: a deep copy, with `undefined` as `null`.
- color: `{ r, g, b, a }` in 0 to 1.
- point, size, anchor, point3d, point4d, and transform: an array of numbers.
- layer: `{ layerId, instance? }` or `null`.
- image, video, and sound: `{ assetId?, url? }` or `null`. When the value holds an asset id, `url` is filled from `ctx.services.resolveAssetUrl`.
- gradient, shape, textStyle, and layerEffect: deep copies of the runtime objects, or `null`.

**Conversions, script to engine** (`patch.output`):
- `undefined` is rejected for every type. `null` gives the zero value (CONVENTIONS §8) for value types, and `null` for layer, media, gradient, shape, textStyle, and layerEffect.
- number: a finite number, `true`/`false` as 1/0, or a numeric string. index: the same, truncated toward zero, with negatives as 0. boolean: JavaScript truthiness. text: a string as is, numbers and booleans through `String`, and objects and arrays through `JSON.stringify`.
- enum: a declared option key. json: plain data (objects, arrays, strings, finite numbers, booleans, `null`). Functions and `undefined` members are dropped the way `JSON.stringify` drops them, and cycles or non-finite numbers are rejected.
- color: `{ r, g, b, a? }` with `a` defaulting to 1, or `"#RGB"`, `"#RRGGBB"`, or `"#RRGGBBAA"`. Channels clamp to 0 to 1.
- Vectors: an array of the type's length, one number applied to every component, or `{ x, y, z?, w? }`; size also accepts `{ width, height }`. transform: 16 numbers. A non-finite component rejects the value.
- layer: `{ layerId, instance? }` or a layer id string.
- image, video, and sound: `{ assetId }`, `{ url }`, or a URL string.
- shape: `{ path }` or an SVG path string. gradient: `{ kind: "linear" | "radial" | "angular", stops: [{ offset, color }], start, end }`, with stop colors converted as above. layerEffect: `{ kind, params }`. textStyle: an object holding only `TextStyleValue` fields.
- A rejected value keeps the output's previous value and logs `warn` once per restart per output: `<patchId>.<key>: couldn't use <short preview> as <type>, so the output keeps its previous value.`
- wholeLoop outputs: an array becomes a loop of converted items. An item that fails becomes the zero value, with one warning. Any other value becomes a one-item loop. Items past 10,000 are dropped with one warning.

**Timers.**
- `setTimeout(fn, ms, ...args)` and `setInterval(fn, ms, ...args)` return integer ids per instance, starting at 1. A string callback throws `TypeError`.
- Scheduling: `due = ctx.time + max(0, ms) / 1000`, where a non-finite `ms` counts as 0, and `notBeforeFrame = ctx.frame + 1`, so a timer never fires in the frame that created it.
- A timeout fires once, on the first frame where `ctx.time >= due`.
- An interval fires at most once per frame, then advances `due` by its interval until `due > ctx.time`, so a long frame never causes a burst. An interval of `ms <= 0` fires every frame.
- `clearTimeout` and `clearInterval` accept either kind of id and ignore unknown ids.
- Timers read the prototype clock, so they pause while the viewer is paused and replay identically in simulation. A timer fires on the first frame at or after its due time, so at 120 fps it can fire up to one frame earlier than at 60 fps.

**Network.**
- `fetch(url, init?)` resolves to `{ ok, status, url, text(), json() }`.
- `init` supports `method` (default `"GET"`), `headers` (an object or `[name, value]` pairs), `body`, and `signal` from an `AbortController`. A string body is sent as is. A plain object or array body is JSON-encoded, and `Content-Type: application/json` is added when missing.
- Only absolute `http:` and `https:` URLs are allowed. Anything else rejects with `TypeError("Scripts can only fetch http or https URLs.")`.
- The host calls `ctx.services.platform.fetch(url, { method, headers, body, signal })` during the invocation and reads the whole body with `text()`. The host request is aborted when the script's signal aborts, the instance stalls, or the prototype restarts. `response.headers` offers `get(name)`, `has(name)`, and `forEach`, with case-insensitive names. When that settles, the result is queued and delivered at the start of the next frame's step, never mid-frame. `text()` and `json()` resolve during that delivery, and `json()` rejects with `SyntaxError` for invalid JSON.
- When `platform.fetch` is missing, or the host hasn't granted this document network access for scripts, the promise rejects with `Error("Network isn't available for scripts here.")`. Transport failures reject with `TypeError("Network request failed")`.
- Limits: 32 requests in flight per instance (the next one rejects), and 10 MB per response body.
- `controller.abort()` rejects the promise with an error named `AbortError` on the next step, and the host result is dropped when it arrives.
- The web player follows browser CORS rules. The desktop app may route requests without them.

**Errors.**
- Compile errors: a syntax error, or an exception while running top-level code, sets `compileError`. It raises a runtime issue `{ code: "script_error", severity: "error", patchId }` with the message `scripts/<file>:<line>:<column> <message>` through `ctx.services.issue`, which the Diagnostics tab and the node badge show. It isn't also logged, because `ctx.services.log("error", ...)` would file a second, `patch_error` issue. Nothing retries until the source changes or the prototype restarts. Outputs hold their last committed values, or their defaults.
- An exception thrown synchronously from `evaluate` or a timer callback discards the outputs and pulses that invocation staged, and raises the same issue with the script line. The next trigger runs `evaluate` again.
- Writes from promise callbacks commit as each callback returns. An unhandled rejection is logged as an error.
- Each distinct error message is logged once per instance per restart.
- `console.log`, `info`, `warn`, `error`, and `debug` go through `ctx.services.log` (`info` and `debug` map to `log`), prefixed `[<patchId>#<loopIndex>]`. The limit is 100 messages per instance per frame, followed by one "more messages hidden" line.

**Loops.**
- **Per-item mode** (no declared port has `wholeLoop`): the engine evaluates once per loop index, and each index gets its own instance with its own module scope, timers, requests, and outputs.
  - New indices start fresh: the top level runs, then `evaluate` runs on that frame.
  - Removed indices are disposed: their timers are cleared and their pending results dropped.
  - Output length follows the engine rule: the longest input loop, with shorter loops wrapping and scalars broadcasting.
  - Above 1,000 instances, log one warning suggesting whole-loop mode.
- **Whole-loop mode** (any declared port has `wholeLoop: true`): the definePatch module marks those ports `wholeLoop`, and one instance serves the patch.
  - `patch.inputItems` returns each input whole, at its own length, with no wrapping; an empty loop gives `[]`.
  - Non-wholeLoop outputs are single values, and wholeLoop outputs are loops.
  - `patch.loopIndex` is 0.

**Frame 0.** An instance is created during its first evaluation: top-level code runs, then `evaluate` runs with the authored inputs. `patch.changed` is false for every key, and a pulse arriving on frame 0 shows through `patch.pulsed`. Outputs not yet written show their declared `default`, or the type's zero value.

**Retargeting.**
- Input changes never cancel anything by themselves. Timers and requests keep going until the script clears or aborts them.
- Changing the script source or `typeParam` rebuilds every instance: timers are cleared, pending results dropped, and module scope starts over.
- After a rebuild, outputs keep their last committed values, except outputs whose key or type changed, which start from their defaults.

**Muted.**
- No script code runs: no top level for new instances, no `evaluate`, no timers, and no deliveries. Instances keep their module state.
- Outputs follow the default bypass: each output passes through the first input of the same type, other outputs emit zero values, and no pulses fire.
- On the first unmuted frame, timers that came due fire once (intervals realign), and settled requests are delivered.

**Platform and simulation.**
- The engine is plain ECMAScript on WebAssembly, so the patch works in the desktop app, in desktop and mobile browsers, and in Node. Only `fetch` depends on the host.
- In deterministic runtimes, randomness, dates, and timers come from engine services. A host that stubs `platform.fetch` must let stub promises settle before each `step` (await between steps), so deliveries land on the same frame every run.
- A script's only effects outside the sandbox are `fetch` and log messages.

**Restart and dispose.**
- Restart disposes every instance: timers are cleared, pending results dropped, and contexts freed. Outputs, stalled flags, and error and warning deduplication all reset.
- New instances are created on the new run's frame 0.
- A compiled-bytecode cache keyed by source text may survive restarts.
- `dispose` frees the engine runtime and everything it holds.

**Runtime contract.**
- `dynamicPorts(node, doc)` builds ports from `doc.scripts`; `evaluate` reads the source through `ctx.services.readScript(file)` and reparses the header only when the file or source changes.
- `dynamicPorts` returns the script's `variants`, so core accepts the typeParams a script declares and the node switches type like a built-in patch.
- Budgets use `ctx.services.deterministic`: interrupt-check counting in deterministic runtimes, wall-clock time otherwise.
- A broken header can only throw from `dynamicPorts`, which leaves the patch with no ports until the header is fixed (`dynamicPortsRule`).

**Coming from Origami.**
- Detection: a file that has no `export` at the top level and constructs `new Patch()` runs in compatibility mode. The file body is wrapped as `(function () { ... })()` and must return that patch object.
- Extra globals: `Patch`, `PatchInput`, `PatchOutput`, `types`, `Http`, `Base64`, and `console.watch`, which logs its value.
- Declarations: `patch.inputs` and `patch.outputs` are arrays of `new PatchInput(name, types.X, default?)` and `new PatchOutput(...)`. They're read statically along with `patch.variants`, `patch.loopAware`, and `patch.alwaysNeedsToEvaluate` (`dynamicPortsRule`). `loopAware = true` makes every port `wholeLoop`, and `alwaysNeedsToEvaluate` maps to `alwaysEvaluate`.
- Types: NUMBER → number; PROGRESS → number with subtype progress; INTEGER → number with step 1; POSITION → point; SIZE → size; ANCHOR → anchor; POINT3D → point3d; POINT4D → point4d; COLOR → color; BOOLEAN → boolean; PULSE → pulse; ENUM → index, because the file carries no option names; STRING → text; JSON → json; IMAGE → image; VARIANT → variant.
- Values: vectors are `{ x, y, z?, w? }` (SIZE uses x for width and y for height), and colors are `{ x: r, y: g, z: b, w: a }`.
- Reading and writing ports: `patch.inputs[i].value` and `.values`. `isDirty()` is true when the value changed since this instance's previous `evaluate`. `readRising()` is true when a pulse fired or the value became truthy since then, and `readFalling()` when it became falsy. `patch.outputs[i].value = ...`, `.values = [...]`, and `.pulse()` write outputs. `patch.type` is the active variant as the constant name, such as "POSITION".
- `Http.request`, `get`, `post`, `getJson`, and `postJson` are built on `fetch`, with `headers`, `urlParameters`, and `body`. The options `responseType`, `onData`, and `contentType: "formData"` reject with "isn't supported yet".
- `Base64.encode(text)` and `Base64.decode(text)` handle UTF-8 text. ArrayBuffer and image targets reject.
- `Image` pixel methods throw "Reading and writing pixels isn't supported yet."
- Differences:
  - Cables match by key, where Origami matches ports by position. The derived keys in `dynamicPortsRule` keep imported wiring stable.
  - Duplicating a patch copies its script, as in current Origami.
  - `evaluate` always runs on an instance's first frame. Origami's first-run timing is undocumented.

settings.name: Script
settings.description: The script file in the project's scripts folder, like "email_check.js". Empty means there's no script yet, so the patch has no ports.

patches.dynamicPortsRule:
Ports come from the script's header. It's read without running any code, so core can validate ops headlessly and synchronously. 1. **Find the source.** `file = node.settings?.script ?? ""`. When it's empty, return `{ inputs: [], outputs: [] }`. Otherwise `source = doc.scripts[file]`. An undefined source throws `Error("scripts/ doesn't exist. Create it with setScript or choose another file.")`, and a source over 1 MB throws. 2. **Tokenize** with a JavaScript-aware tokenizer that tracks line and column. It must handle: - line and block comments; - `'` and `"` strings with escapes, and template literals; - regular-expression literals: a `/` starts one unless the previous token is an identifier, number, string, `)`, or `]`; - numbers, identifiers, and punctuation. 3. **Native header.** Skip leading whitespace, comments, a hashbang, and a `"use strict"` directive. - Read statements of the form `export const = `, ended by `;` or a line break. `` is `inputs`, `outputs`, `variants`, or `alwaysEvaluate`, and each may appear once. - Stop at the first statement of any other form. - If one of those names is exported later in the file, throw "Move export const above the other code so Sonobe can read the ports without running the script." 4. **Compatibility mode** applies when no `export` token appears at brace depth 0 and the source contains `new Patch(`. - Read the depth-0 statements `

.inputs = [ ... ]`, `

.outputs = [ ... ]`, `

.variants = [types.X, ...]`, `

.loopAware = `, and `

.alwaysNeedsToEvaluate = `. `

` is the identifier assigned `new Patch()` with `var`, `let`, or `const`. - Items are `new PatchInput(, types., ?)` or `new PatchOutput(...)`. Map the types as in `behavior`. - The key is the camelCase form of the name: words split on anything but letters and digits, so `"Email Address"` becomes `emailAddress`, and a leading digit gets the prefix `port`. An empty name or a key that's already taken falls back to `input` or `output`, where n is the 1-based position. - The display name is the given name, or "Input n" / "Output n" when it's empty. 5. **Literal grammar** (a JSON5-like subset; comments are allowed between tokens): ``` literal := object | array | string | number | "true" | "false" | "null" object := "{" (member ("," member)* ","?)? "}" member := (IDENT | string) ":" literal array := "[" (literal ("," literal)* ","?)? "]" string := '...' | "..." | `...` containing no ${ number := "-"? (digits ("." digits)? | "." digits) exponent? | "0x" hexdigits ``` Anything else, such as identifiers other than `true`, `false`, and `null`, calls, spreads, operators, or `${`, throws "Write the port list as plain values. at line L isn't allowed here." 6. **Validate.** - `inputs` and `outputs` are arrays of at most 32 port objects each. - Fields: `key` (required; matches `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`; unique across inputs and outputs), `type` (required), plus optional `name`, `subtype`, `default`, `min`, `max`, `step`, `enumOptions`, `description`, `wholeLoop`, and `advanced`. - An unknown field throws with a did-you-mean. - `type` is one of `number, boolean, pulse, text, color, point, point3d, point4d, size, anchor, index, enum, json, layer, image, video, sound, gradient, shape, textStyle, layerEffect, transform` or `variant`. `any` throws with a hint to use `json` or `variant`. - `variant` ports require `variants`: at least 2 distinct allowed types, excluding `pulse`, `enum`, and `variant`. A `variants` list with no variant port is ignored. - `enum` ports require `enumOptions`: 1 to 256 entries. Each entry is a string, used as both key and name, or a `{ key, name?, description? }` object. Keys are unique and match the key pattern. - `default` uses the document encoding for its type (CONVENTIONS §7), and pulse ports take none. - An enum default must be an option key. - A variant port's default must fit the active variant, or the zero value is used. - On an output, `default` is the value shown before the first write. - `subtype` must be a `ValueSubtype`. - `min`, `max`, and `step` must be finite, with `min <= max` and `step > 0`. - `wholeLoop`, `advanced`, `alwaysEvaluate`, `loopAware`, and `alwaysNeedsToEvaluate` must be booleans. - Every problem throws `Error("scripts/:: ")`, which core reports as `dynamic_ports_failed`. 7. **Build `PortSpec`s** in declaration order. - `name` defaults to the key split into Title Case words: `itemCount` becomes "Item Count", and `max_speed` becomes "Max Speed". - `description` defaults to `""`. - A `variant` type resolves to the active variant: `node.typeParam` when `variants` lists it, otherwise the first variant. - An input `default` defaults to the type's zero value (CONVENTIONS §8). Output PortSpecs omit `default`, which the runtime keeps for initial output values. 8. **Memoize** results by `(source, typeParam)` in a bounded LRU of 64 entries. - **Cables follow keys.** Changing a port's `name` keeps its cables. Changing its `key`, or removing the port, leaves stored inputs as `unknown_port` diagnostics and downstream links dangling. Nothing is deleted automatically, because script files can change outside ops, for example in an external editor or through git. Tools that edit a script should add cleanup ops to the same batch, so one undo restores everything. - **Batch order.** `setScript` must come before any `addPatch` inputs, `setInput`, or `connect` that uses the script's ports, because ops validate ports as they apply.
commonMistakes: The patch has no ports and warns that it couldn't work out its ports: the inputs or outputs list uses a variable or a function call, or sits below other code. Put export const inputs = [...] and export const outputs = [...] at the top of the file, written as plain values.

An output updates once and then freezes even though the script tracks time: evaluate runs only when an input changes or a pulse arrives. Call patch.requestNextFrame() while something is moving, or add export const alwaysEvaluate = true.
Cables disappear after you edit the script: you changed a port's key, and cables follow keys. Change the port's name instead to relabel it and keep its connections.
A loop of 50 items makes 50 network requests: in a loop, the script runs once per item. Mark the port wholeLoop: true to receive the whole loop at once and make one request.

examples.title: Tap to load a new quote
examples.description: quotes.js declares a load pulse input plus quote (text) and loading (boolean) outputs. When patch.pulsed("load") is true, it sets loading, fetches JSON from a quotes service, writes the quote, and clears loading. The Transition dims the text while a request is out.
examples.outline:
layer quote text "Quote" @24,200 354x240 text←quotes.quote opacity←dim.output
layer load_button rectangle "Load Button" @24,720 354x56 cornerRadius=28 color=#5B5FEFFF
patch tap_load interaction layer=@load_button
patch quotes javascript script="quotes.js" load←tap_load.tap
patch dim transition<number> progress←quotes.loading start=1 end=0.4

examples.title: Draw a trail behind your finger
examples.description: trail.js declares position (point) and down (boolean) inputs and a shape output. A top-level array keeps the last 40 positions while down is true, and evaluate turns them into an SVG path such as M 120 300 L 124 306.
examples.outline:
layer trail shape "Trail" @0,0 402x874 shape←trail_path.shape color=#00000000 strokeColor=#5B5FEFFF strokeWidth=6
layer touch_area hitArea "Touch Area" @0,0 402x874
patch touch interaction layer=@touch_area
patch trail_path javascript script="trail.js" position←touch.position down←touch.down

defaultNotes.script: sonobe: Origami inserts a patch with no script until a file is dropped or chosen; Sonobe's editor and MCP create a starter file named after the patch id, and empty means no script yet.
